channel.title: Frimley Fuel Allotments — Timeline of Events
channel.description: A fully sourced public records timeline tracking the proposed development of the Frimley Fuel Allotments woodland and Pine Ridge Golf Club for a new Frimley Park Hospital. Compiled from publicly available sources only.

item.title: 21 March 2023 — Gove, Docherty and Sunderland write jointly to Health Secretary describing new-site build as "the Trust's preferred way forward"
item.description: Michael Gove MP (Surrey Heath), Leo Docherty MP (Aldershot), and James Sunderland MP (Bracknell) write jointly to Health Secretary Steve Barclay offering "wholehearted support" for Frimley Health's £1.26bn New Hospital Programme bid. The letter describes a new-site build as "the Trust's preferred way forward" — adopting the Trust's own framing eight months before Frimley Health would open a public consultation on site selection criteria. At the time of writing, Gove is simultaneously the constituency MP for Surrey Heath and Secretary of State for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities, the government department responsible for national planning policy. HWRA meeting minutes record that around the same period, Gove is reported to have indicated to those with an interest in the process that Frimley Fuel Allotments was the likely site — before any formal site selection process had begun. Source: Michael Gove MP, Leo Docherty MP, James Sunderland MP, joint letter to Rt Hon Steve Barclay MP, 21 March 2023; HWRA meeting minutes, 3 July 2026.

item.title: 30 October 2026 — As McCarthy discourages formal letters, Pinkerton formally writes to the Secretary of State seeking clarification on the hospital's funding after a £957m procurement correction
item.description: On the same day FHFT Chief Executive Lance McCarthy writes to Dr Al Pinkerton MP encouraging him to use private phone calls rather than formal correspondence, Pinkerton writes formally to the Secretary of State for Health and Social Care, Yvette Cooper MP, seeking clarification on the procurement notice amendment filed two days earlier. The letter centres on a specific discrepancy: the Government's NHP implementation plan (January 2025) placed Frimley Park Hospital in the £1.5 billion to £2 billion estimated cost category, with around £1.8 billion understood to apply to the build itself. The 28 October amendment to the Hospital 2.0 Alliance contract — described only as "error identified by NHP" — records the corrected value as £1.043 billion, a reduction of nearly £957 million. Pinkerton also notes that separate procurement documents had listed the contract value at £200 billion. He asks four specific questions about the funding, scope, approved budget and any restrictions on hospital size or timetable, and calls for a published reconciliation of the procurement and programme figures. Sources: Dr Al Pinkerton MP, letter to the Rt Hon Yvette Cooper MP, Secretary of State for Health and Social Care, 30 October 2026; Al Pinkerton MP Facebook, 30 October 2026.

item.title: 30 October 2026 — McCarthy concedes hybrid planning approach — and tells Pinkerton to stop writing letters
item.description: FHFT Chief Executive Lance McCarthy responds to Dr Al Pinkerton MP's letter of 21 October 2026. On planning, he confirms the Trust will pursue a hybrid planning application, stating an outline application "is not, and never has been, our preferred approach" — a concession to the position Pinkerton had explicitly pressed for. The Trust had not previously made this public. More strikingly, McCarthy tells Pinkerton to stop using formal correspondence: "I would again encourage you to raise questions like these directly with me or members of the programme team here, either by phone or at one of our regular meetings, rather than dealing with them through an exchange of letters." A formal letter from an MP to a public NHS body creates a record that can be published, submitted to scrutiny committees and verified. A phone call creates none of these things. McCarthy published this letter on FHFT's own website — putting on the public record his request that the MP should avoid doing the same. Source: Lance McCarthy, letter to Dr Al Pinkerton MP, 30 October 2026 — fhft.nhs.uk

item.title: 2 October 2026 — As engagement runs, AECOM is appointed both project manager and cost consultant for the new hospital — the professional team for a settled site is complete
item.description: Two F03 contract award notices published on 2 October 2026 — ten days before the public engagement closes — reveal that AECOM Limited has been appointed to two senior roles on the New Frimley Park Hospital programme, both via the HPCCAS framework without open competition. AECOM is appointed Cost Consultant (£477,891.94, awarded 23 September 2026) and Project Manager (£1,186,950, awarded 30 September 2026). Together with Arcadis (architect, appointed 13 August), Sacyr (construction contract signed 30 July), and the planning and legal tenders already published, this completes the core professional team required to develop, design, and obtain planning permission for a specific site. The combined value of appointments made before the engagement closed exceeds £9 million. Professional teams of this kind are appointed for named projects on defined sites — not to explore whether a site might be chosen. When McCarthy told ITV on 13 October that the site was "absolutely" still open to challenge, the project manager and cost consultant had each been in post for nearly a fortnight. Sources: Find a Tender, Notice 2026/S 000-093424 and Notice 2026/S 000-093426, published 2 October 2026.

item.title: 16 September 2026 — FHFT tenders £1 million planning lawyers contract — with bids accepted on the day the engagement exercise closes
item.description: Nine days after publishing the town planner tender, FHFT publishes a contract for specialist town planning legal advice (Notice 2026/S 000-087608), estimated at £1,000,000 excluding VAT. The scope covers the full legal apparatus to obtain planning permission: planning applications, EIA and HRA legal advice, Section 106 negotiation, and — explicitly — "judicial review and statutory challenge advice under the Town and Country Planning Act 1990." The tender submission deadline was 12 October 2026 — the final day of the public engagement exercise. Legally binding bids from law firms were accepted at the same moment the Trust closed the public inbox. The following day, 13 October, McCarthy was asked by ITV whether the site location was "still genuinely open to challenge" and answered: "Yes, absolutely." A planning consent process cannot be underway for a site that has not been chosen. Source: Find a Tender, Notice 2026/S 000-087608, published 16 September 2026.

item.title: 7 September 2026 — On the day of its public engagement webinar, FHFT publishes a tender for a seven-year town planning contract — including Environmental Impact Assessment and Habitats Regulations Assessment for the FFA site
item.description: On the same day that Frimley Health holds its public engagement webinar, the Trust publishes a formal tender notice on the government's Find a Tender register (Notice 2026/S 000-084205) seeking a provider for "the provision of town planning services in connection with the New Frimley Park Hospital programme." The scope covers the full planning consent pipeline including EIA co-ordination, Habitats Regulations Assessment, Section 106 negotiation, and post-consent support — statutory processes triggered by a settled development proposal, not a live deliberation. The contract runs from 24 November 2026 to 31 December 2033 (seven years). The tender submission deadline was 7 October 2026, five days before the engagement exercise closed on 12 October. Award decision date: 4 November 2026. Estimated contract value: £221,000 excluding VAT. Source: Find a Tender, Notice 2026/S 000-084205, published 7 September 2026.

item.title: 28 October 2026 — NHS England quietly corrects Frimley hospital contract notice after £957m error — official government register confirms £1.043bn contract, with just £3.4m currently authorised
item.description: Seven days after Frimley Health NHS Foundation Trust publishes the formal contract award notice for the new hospital on the government's Find a Tender register — filing the contract value at £2,000,000,000 — the New Hospital Programme files two amendment releases on 28 October 2026, correcting the figure to £1,043,000,000. The difference is exactly £957,000,000. The reason given on the official government procurement register: "Error identified by NHP." The original notice also listed the lowest and highest bid as £200,000,000,000 — two hundred billion pounds — a separate error on the same document. The corrected notice confirms that only £3,404,000 is currently authorised (Stage Zero advisory works); the £1.043bn headline figure requires further Notices to Proceed for Stages One and Two before any building can begin. Source: UK government procurement register, OCDS release package ocds-h6vhtk-044e56, 28 October 2026; Construction News, 29 October 2026.

item.title: 9 December 2025 — JHOSC Chair warns NHS scrutiny "catastrophe" if independent oversight abolished — calls letting NHS assess itself "marking their own homework"
item.description: At a meeting of Surrey County Council's Adult and Health Select Committee, Cllr Trefor Hogg — who chairs both that committee and the JHOSC responsible for scrutinising the Frimley Park Hospital relocation — moves a motion calling on the DHSC to reverse its plans to abolish local Healthwatch organisations. The motion passes unanimously with full cross-party support. Hogg warns that without independent patient representation, NHS and social care services "will not face proper scrutiny in the future" and that ministers will be able to "mark their own homework." He describes the loss of independent local oversight as "a catastrophe in the making." Seven months later, as JHOSC Chair for the FFA scrutiny process, Hogg pre-shares his committee's questions with NHS representatives privately before public meetings, co-signs a letter on behalf of the JHOSC without committee authority to prevent formal public consultation, and dismisses campaign concerns as "misplaced claims" — conduct that the SCC Monitoring Officer subsequently confirms exceeded his authority. Source: Trefor Hogg, Facebook post, 9 December 2025; BBC Surrey, Jack Fiehn, 15 December 2025.

item.title: 24 December 2025 — Elected councillor publicly denies any formal sale agreement — weeks before option signed
item.description: Writing to a local resident on Christmas Eve 2025, Councillor Murray Rowlands states that "nothing has been decided about whether a sale of the Fuel Allotment's land at Pine Ridge will take place" and that "there has not been a formal offer nor has the Trust moved to accept any offer to alienate its land to Frimley Park Hospital." The letter was written just 23 days before the Option to Purchase agreement was formally signed on 16 January 2026. Rowlands also states that only a "small part" of the allotment would be used for construction and car parking — a characterisation at odds with the Trust's own engagement materials, which describe a 55-acre development footprint in a predominantly wooded site. Source: Councillor Murray Rowlands, letter to local resident, 24 December 2025.

item.title: July 2026 — School trust formally objects to Pine Ridge — warns process has "reached a conclusion before key questions have been fully assessed"
item.description: Engage Enrich Excel Academies Trust (EEEA) — whose schools include Ravenscote Junior School, the educational setting closest to the proposed site — writes formally to Frimley Health raising significant concerns. The letter warns that the selection process "appears to have reached a conclusion before key questions relating to road capacity, emergency access, school travel, pedestrian safety and infrastructure requirements have been fully assessed." On community engagement, EEEA states that "the limited engagement to date risks creating the perception that consultation is being undertaken to support a preferred outcome rather than genuinely shape the decision-making process." The letter cites Chobham Road and Old Bisley Road as already experiencing significant congestion during school hours, with the road network becoming "effectively gridlocked" during M3 incidents. Source: Engage Enrich Excel Academies Trust, letter to Caroline Hutton, Frimley Health NHS Foundation Trust, July 2026.

item.title: 21 October 2026 — McCarthy publicly confirms Frimley Fuel Allotments as preferred site in open letter to Surrey Heath school leaders
item.description: FHFT Chief Executive Lance McCarthy publishes a formal response to Surrey Heath school leaders on the Trust's own website — the first time FHFT has confirmed the designation in its own words on a public-facing platform: "Land currently occupied by Pine Ridge Golf Club, owned by local charity Frimley Fuel Allotments, is our preferred site." McCarthy frames "preferred site" as a Green Book process term, notes it is not a final decision, and states it follows a review of 18 other sites and two rounds of independent analysis. He confirms a third-party consultant is carrying out transport analysis this autumn and winter working directly with headteachers. He acknowledges school leaders remain opposed — "you remain opposed to the site, and there is more work to do together" — and adds: "I also recognise that your experience of our discussions to date may differ from how they have been described publicly." Source: Lance McCarthy, open letter to Surrey Heath school leaders, 21 October 2026 (fhft.nhs.uk).

item.title: 21 October 2026 — Pinkerton writes to McCarthy urging hybrid planning application — warns outline route would defer "potentially determinative" questions on site viability
item.description: Dr Al Pinkerton MP writes to FHFT Chief Executive Lance McCarthy urging the Trust to submit a hybrid planning application rather than a wholly outline one. Pinkerton argues that transport, access and highways are not secondary reserved matters — they go directly to whether Frimley Fuel Allotments is a viable location at all. A wholly outline application would allow the principle of development to be established while deferring the most consequential questions to later reserved matters applications. Pinkerton warns: "The planning process should be the point at which those questions are exposed to proper scrutiny — not a mechanism through which they are deferred." Source: Dr Al Pinkerton MP, letter to Lance McCarthy, 21 October 2026.

item.title: 17 October 2026 — Hogg newsletter admits access problems "undoubtedly real and present right now"
item.description: JHOSC Chair Cllr Trefor Hogg's ward newsletter confirms that the Transport and Access Study for the FFA site is only now "getting under way," with winter data still needed. He writes that access problems are "undoubtedly real and present right now" — directly contradicting his co-signed letter to NHS Frimley ICB of 4 July 2025, which asserted there would be "no negative impact on access." That letter was cited by the ICB when resolving not to undertake public consultation — a resolution the SCC Monitoring Officer has since confirmed was issued without authority and carried "no weight." The newsletter also confirms the scheme is moving from Strategic Outline Case to Outline Business Case stage, and that land purchases are expected before the Full Business Case is approved. Source: Trefor Hogg ward newsletter, 17 October 2026.

item.title: 14 October 2026 — SHBC Leader confirms monitoring officer ruled JHOSC letter had "no weight"
item.description: At Surrey Heath Borough Council's Full Council meeting, Council Leader Cllr Shaun Macdonald states that FHFT is "playing a little bit fast and loose with the facts" on school engagement. He then makes a statement of major legal significance: "The monitoring officer from Surrey County Council has confirmed that the chair and vice chair had no such authority to write on behalf of that body and therefore that letter had no weight in the decision-making process." The letter — co-signed by JHOSC Chair Cllr Trefor Hogg and Vice-Chair Cllr Carla Morson — was used by NHS Frimley ICB as the basis for its July 2025 resolution not to undertake public consultation. Macdonald also warns that if the proposal proceeds, "there will, on a mathematical and risk basis, there will be fatalities and serious injuries." Source: SHBC Full Council, 14 October 2026.

item.title: 13 October 2026 — ICO rules FHFT breached environmental information law on the day engagement closes
item.description: The Information Commissioner's Office issues Decision Notice IC-567662-H7C3 finding that Frimley Health NHS Foundation Trust breached Regulation 5(2) of the Environmental Information Regulations 2004 by failing to respond within 20 working days to a request for all documentation, environmental reports, traffic and infrastructure reports, and risk maps relating to the site decision — submitted on 15 June 2026, the day before the preferred site was publicly announced. The ICO orders FHFT to provide a substantive response within 30 calendar days. Failure to comply may be treated as contempt of court. The notice is issued on the same day the 17-week public engagement closes — meaning residents completed their responses without access to documentation the Trust was legally required to disclose. Source: ICO Decision Notice IC-567662-H7C3, 13 October 2026.

item.title: 13 October 2026 — FHFT confirms 10,000 responses as 17-week engagement closes — planning application and JHOSC scrutiny timetable set
item.description: Frimley Health NHS Foundation Trust announces the close of its 17-week public engagement on 12 October 2026, confirming more than 10,000 responses across 23 postcode areas in Surrey, Hampshire and Berkshire. An independent analysis by Opinion Research Services (ORS) is now underway; findings are to be published in a report later this year and presented to the Joint Health Overview and Scrutiny Committee at the end of November 2026. FHFT confirms a planning application is planned for autumn 2027, with national approvals and detailed business cases required before any construction can begin. Traffic surveys will be carried out over the coming winter. Chief Executive Lance McCarthy acknowledges that feedback included "concerns about issues such as traffic at the preferred location" and commits to working with communities to "develop solutions to areas of concern and challenge." Source: FHFT, "Public engagement on proposals for a new Frimley Park Hospital comes to a close," 13 October 2026 (fhft.nhs.uk).

item.title: 13 October 2026 — Pinkerton tells ITV of 50-acre sites "not even considered" — McCarthy confirms surveys still outstanding
item.description: ITV News broadcasts a report on the proposed new Frimley Park Hospital. CEO Lance McCarthy confirms traffic, transport and ecological surveys have not yet been completed. Dr Al Pinkerton MP tells ITV he is aware of "50 acre sites, which is what they claim they need, that haven't even been considered" — directly challenging the credibility of the 18-site selection process. When pressed whether the location is "still genuinely open to challenge," McCarthy answers: "Yes, absolutely." Source: ITV News, 13 October 2026.

item.title: 8 October 2026 — Windlesham Parish Council warns communities must not become "rat-runs" — criticises late engagement
item.description: Windlesham Parish Council submits a formal consultation response on behalf of the communities of Bagshot, Lightwater and Windlesham. Without opposing the principle of a new hospital, the Council raises significant concerns on transport and engagement. It demands traffic modelling covering the A322/M3 Junction 3 interchange, peak-period conditions, long-term demand, and displacement through all three villages, warning they "must not become rat-runs." It states that reduced car dependency must not substitute for proper road capacity assessment. On engagement: "That has not been our experience" — and: "Communication should not simply be about explaining decisions that have already been made." Source: Windlesham Parish Council, consultation response, 8 October 2026.

item.title: 12 October 2026 — 36 schools and 13,000 pupils: updated joint statement opposes FFA site on day engagement closes
item.description: On the day the public engagement exercise closes, school leaders from more than 36 schools covering 13,000+ pupils issue an updated joint statement opposing the FFA site. Their message: "We support the urgent delivery of a new Frimley Park Hospital. We do not support the Frimley Fuel Allotments site." The statement directly contradicts FHFT's public claim of close collaboration with schools: "public statements have suggested there has been close collaboration with school leaders when this has not reflected our experience." Dr Al Pinkerton MP says the case for the FFA site "has not been made." Sources: Local School Leaders joint statement; Al Pinkerton MP, Facebook, 12 October 2026.

item.title: 12 October 2026 — Public engagement closes — 10,000+ responses received, but traffic study has not yet started
item.description: The 17-week public engagement exercise closes. CEO Lance McCarthy tells BBC Radio Berkshire the programme received over 10,000 questionnaire responses. He confirms detailed traffic and transport analysis will not begin until November 2026 — after the engagement has closed — meaning residents raised transport concerns without access to any completed transport modelling for the site. HWRA members are quoted by BBC Surrey highlighting dangers to pedestrians and the community value of the woodland. Sources: BBC Radio Berkshire; BBC News, 12 October 2026.

item.title: 7 October 2026 — FHFT's final engagement email confirms ORS will "not make recommendations or decisions"
item.description: Four days before the engagement deadline, FHFT distributes an email confirming that Opinion Research Services (ORS) will prepare a report but will not make recommendations or decisions on the site. This directly contradicts FHFT's own FAQ, which states the site choice is "not final." The email also introduces the Green Book framework as reassurance — drawing attention to the fact that no business case has yet been approved. Source: FHFT email to members, 7 October 2026.

item.title: 29 September 2026 — CEO Facebook reel responds to "key issues raised" — five claims warrant scrutiny
item.description: CEO Lance McCarthy publishes a video responding to key issues raised about the proposed hospital. Analysis of the verbatim transcript identifies five claims that warrant scrutiny: a false dichotomy on the current site, unconfirmed funding presented as secured, an "independently assured" process with no assurance report published, a geographically misleading "closer to home" claim, and a framing that confirms the decision is treated as already made. Source: FHFT Facebook, 29 September 2026.

item.title: 26 September 2026 — JHOSC Chair's newsletter reports Annual Members' Meeting as promotional content — omits deprivation admission
item.description: JHOSC Chair Cllr Trefor Hogg's ward newsletter reports attending the Annual Members' Meeting but omits FHFT's own admission that a rival site scored better on deprivation. The newsletter also states the RAAC deadline as "by 2025" — a year that has passed and a date that appears in none of FHFT's official materials. Source: Trefor Hogg ward newsletter, 26 September 2026.

item.title: 22 September 2026 — At Annual Members' Meeting, FHFT concedes a better site for deprived communities existed — but was set aside
item.description: At FHFT's Annual Members' Meeting, a slide states: "One shortlisted site scored better on deprivation, but it could not be delivered because of size, aviation and ownership constraints." This is a formal, on-the-record concession that the Frimley Fuel Allotments is not the site best placed to serve communities with the highest health need. The evidence for setting aside the better-scoring site has not been published. Sources: FHFT Annual Members' Meeting, 22 September 2026.

item.title: 21 September 2026 — FHFT maildrop reaches local households — proposed site not mentioned
item.description: Frimley Health distributes an engagement postcard to households across its catchment area inviting residents to complete a questionnaire. The leaflet does not mention the Frimley Fuel Allotments, does not state that a preferred site has already been chosen, and does not mention woodland, green belt or the charity status of the land. Residents completing the exercise in good faith had no basis on which to assess the proposal's implications. Source: FHFT engagement postcard, received September 2026.

item.title: 18 September 2026 — CEO video rules out current site — contradicting FHFT's own record
item.description: CEO Lance McCarthy publishes a Facebook Reel stating the current site rebuild "wouldn't be complete by 2035" and that planning consent is "unlikely." Three things directly contradict this: (1) the government's independent assessment found FPH's RAAC planks serviceable to approximately 2040; (2) FHFT itself received planning approval for a four-storey building on the existing site in March 2023; (3) FHFT's own Site Selection Report shows FFA scored third out of four sites. Sources: Facebook Reel, Lance McCarthy, 18 September 2026; Mott MacDonald/DHSC, December 2025; SHBC planning records.

item.title: 12 September 2026 — Hundreds march in protest at FFA site choice
item.description: Hundreds of residents attend a peaceful protest walk organised by the Heatherside Ward Residents' Association (HWRA), gathering outside the existing Frimley Park Hospital. Dr Al Pinkerton MP attends. An HWRA spokesperson states: "The Trust's own experts ranked it third of four, and worst for the environment, yet it became the preferred choice." Sources: Surrey Live, 14 September 2026; Dr Al Pinkerton MP, Facebook, 14 September 2026.

item.title: 7 September 2026 — HWRA meets FHFT leadership — CEO apologises for engagement failures; CPO contradiction exposed
item.description: HWRA representatives meet CEO Lance McCarthy, SRO Caroline Hutton and Programme Director Alex White at Frimley Park Hospital. Key disclosures: McCarthy apologises more than once for not getting the engagement right. NHS England is confirmed to have reviewed and re-run the site selection process. FHFT acknowledges that compulsory purchase orders may be needed for transport — directly contradicting its stated rationale for selecting the site. FHFT confirms large areas of woodland would need to be removed. Source: HWRA Notes of meeting with FHFT, published 30 September 2026.

item.title: 6 September 2024 — Transport assessment completed and given to County Highways — junctions already at capacity
item.description: At the September 2024 JHOSC meeting, Interim Programme Director Cain Thomas discloses that a transport assessment has been completed and submitted to Surrey County Highways. The assessment finds that junctions near the preferred sites are "at capacity and requiring significant infrastructure upgrades." Thomas states the cost of road upgrades "would be part of the new funding envelope." The assessment has never been published. A request for its release has been submitted under the Environmental Information Regulations 2004. Sources: JHOSC minutes, 6 September 2024; Surrey CC Highways (EIR request submitted).
